map.name: Attack Challenge
map.testedVersion: Static source audit only; runtime not executed

bugs.title: Reconnect during preload can bypass the fresh-session inventory wipe
bugs.problem: A player can disconnect before the preload wipe and reconnect after it, carrying ordinary stale items into the new Attack session.
bugs.expected: Every participant entering a fresh Attack session receives the same full inventory reset regardless of reconnect timing.
bugs.observed: The wipe only targets players online at the preload callback, while reconnect and the first buy-phase loadout do not remove ordinary stale items.
reproduction: Carry a recognizable ordinary item before starting an Attack match.
Disconnect before the preload inventory-clear callback runs.
Reconnect after that callback while the session is still preloading.
Confirm the stale item remains when the match reaches the initial buy phase.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Attack performs its full wipe only over players online when preload reaches the clear callback. The preloading reconnect path does not replay that boundary, and the initial buy-phase loadout uses partial managed-item cleanup rather than a full inventory clear.

relevantCode.reason: Owns Attack preload clearing, reconnect recovery, and loadout cleanup behavior.

bugs.suggestedFix: Track the fresh-session inventory reset per player and replay the full clear on reconnect before preload or buy-phase continuation.
mustPreserve: Normal kit-managed item cleanup must retain its current mid-session behavior.

bugs.title: Reconnect bypasses an active combat respawn countdown
bugs.problem: A player can disconnect during the death countdown and reconnect back into active Attack gameplay before the intended respawn delay finishes.
bugs.expected: A reconnecting player with a pending respawn stays in spectator/death state until the existing countdown ends.
bugs.observed: CombatTracker restores the countdown, then GameManager restores survival, loadout, and gameplay position about five ticks later.
reproduction: Start an Attack match and die during active combat.
Disconnect while the respawn countdown is running.
Confirm the player returns to active gameplay before the original countdown finishes.
bugs.aiAnalysis: CombatTracker correctly owns pending respawns and restores spectator state on reconnect. GameManager independently restores active-session state shortly afterward without checking that pending respawn, overwriting the correct death lifecycle.

relevantCode.reason: Contains pending respawn ownership and active-session reconnect recovery.

bugs.suggestedFix: Make GameManager defer to the existing pending-respawn owner before restoring survival, loadout, or gameplay position.
mustPreserve: Normal reconnect outside a pending respawn must continue restoring the active session.

bugs.title: Six playable arenas expose only two concurrent sessions
bugs.problem: Attack presents six playable arena surfaces, but only two can run at once; additional ready groups must queue despite having their own arena.
bugs.expected: Presented independent arena capacity matches delivered concurrency, or the lower limit is explicitly authored as the player-facing capability.
bugs.observed: Six arenas accept parties, but MAX_CONCURRENT_ARENAS limits active ticking-area leases to two and queues the third session.
reproduction: Prepare valid parties in 3 different Attack arenas.
Start the first 2 arenas so both hold active arena leases.
Ready and start the third arena.
Confirm the third group is queued even though its own visible arena is otherwise available.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The selected artifact exposes six independent arena/join surfaces while runtime admission hard-caps arena ticking leases at two. The queue is a mitigation path, not evidence that the six visible arenas were authored to mean only two concurrent sessions.

relevantCode.reason: Defines the six Attack arena surfaces, MAX_CONCURRENT_ARENAS, ticking-area lease admission, and queue feedback.

bugs.suggestedFix: Reduce per-arena residency cost or use another proven simulation strategy so visible arena capacity can run concurrently; keep queueing as overflow handling.
mustPreserve: Arena isolation and existing queue feedback must remain intact.
